updated_claim: Japan's METI, at its Procurement Price Calculation Committee meeting on January 17, 2025, announced the exclusion of large-scale general woody biomass power (10,000 kW / 10 MW or more) and all liquid biomass fuels (all scales) from the FIT and FIP schemes from FY2026 onward. This was formally confirmed in METI's official English-language press release dated March 21, 2025. The policy is NOT a blanket halt on all biomass: sub-10MW woody and agricultural biomass projects remain eligible for FIT/FIP support at ¥24/kWh. The practical effect for the 'demand-cliff' framing is real but scoped: it targets the large-scale imported-fuel plants (the primary consumers of Vietnam wood pellets and Indonesia PKS) that are 10MW+. No new FIT/FIP-supported large biomass plants will be approved from FY2026, eliminating the pipeline of subsidized demand that drove pellet and PKS export growth. The original claim's 'halt acceptance of new biomass FIT projects' language is slightly overbroad — the precise scope is large woody (10MW+) and all liquid biomass, not all biomass universally. The FY2026 cutoff and the policy's existence are confirmed.

sources_found.key_quote: At the meeting of its Procurement Price Calculation Committee held on January 17, 2025, METI expressed its intention to discontinue the support of new large-scale woody biomass and all liquid biomass power plants through the FIT and FIP schemes from FY2026 onward.

METI maintained the FiP and FiT price for small biomass projects at ¥24/kWh for April 2025-March 2026; applies to projects using general woody and agricultural biomass with less than 10MW capacity — confirming the sub-10MW carve-out while large biomass is excluded.

sources_found.key_quote: Japanese-language METI committee document — confirms large biomass (10,000 kW+) on agenda for FIT/FIP phase-out; cited in Japan Energy Hub's January 2025 coverage as background to the FY2026 decision.

research_notes.scope_refinement: NOT all biomass — specifically large woody (10MW+) and all liquid biomass. Sub-10MW woody/agricultural biomass continues under FIT/FIP at ¥24/kWh.
research_notes.demand_cliff_validity: Valid for the relevant import-fuel category: large-scale biomass plants (10MW+) are the primary importers of Vietnam wood pellets and Indonesia PKS. The subsidy pipeline for new such plants ends FY2026.
research_notes.additional_context: METI had not approved any new large biomass FIT/FIP projects since 2017 in practice; Jan 2025 announcement formally codifies this into regulation. Tender capacity for large biomass being reduced from 120MW to 30MW.
